content: Emtricitabine and tenofovir have been detected in human breast milk. Clinical studies conducted on pregnant women have not demonstrated any evidence of fetal risk, making their use generally acceptable during pregnancy. Emtricitabine is classified as a nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor (NRTI). After undergoing phosphorylation, it interferes with the activity of HIV viral DNA polymerase, thereby inhibiting viral replication. It is a cytosine analogue. Tenofovir is also a nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor (NRTI). Following hydrolysis and phosphorylation, it inhibits HIV-1 reverse transcriptase by competing with adenosine monophosphate (AMP) as a substrate. These medications can be taken with or without food. Tablets should be swallowed whole and must not be chewed, crushed, broken, or dissolved. Adding plans allows for the comparison of formulary status with other drugs in the same therapeutic class.
